faq.q: How does the robot plan routes?
alts: how does the robot avoid obstacles
faq.text: The robot plans routes with an A* search on a virtual floor map, using 8-connected cells with no corner cutting, a step limit of 0.18 m, and a cost that keeps it centered in aisles [DOC-APP-NAV]. A cell is walkable only if it is observed floor and has more than 0.20 m of clearance from the distance transform, and the path is then smoothed only inside walkable cells [DOC-APP-NAV]. The route is validated by resampling about every 2.5 cm and checking for collisions and minimum clearance [DOC-APP-NAV].

faq.q: What is fouling in a process pump?
faq.text:
In a process pump, fouling means internal deposits or build-up are narrowing the hydraulic path, so the pump moves less liquid and loses efficiency. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] 
The training notes link fouling to the casing or impeller, with signs like lower flow, lower pressure, or higher motor current for the same duty. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] 
In the fleet table, P-005 is marked as a process pump with issue fouling and an efficiency-loss summary, which matches that general meaning. [ASSET-017]

faq.q: What is cavitation risk?
faq.text: Cavitation risk is a hydraulic instability that can make a process pump behave like it is starving or flashing, and the evidence marks it as high severity or medium severity depending on the case [CASE-049] [CASE-026] [CASE-022]. The related pump note says cavitation can cause erosion at the impeller vane inlets and pitting in the volute casing, with symptoms tied to flow, pressure, motor current, and vibration signals [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#impeller] [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#casing]. For the selected fleet, P-002 has a cavitation risk issue and attention required status, with high urgency and 14 open alarms/events [ASSET-014]. The tool cannot judge whether the asset is safe; that decision belongs to site procedures and qualified personnel, with verification and escalation under lockout/tagout [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY].

faq.q: What does misalignment look like in the data?
faq.text:
Misalignment looks like a rotating-equipment alignment signature with vibration, often axial or at 2×, and it may also show element wear or higher motor current. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#coupling] 
For pumps and motors, the data pattern is usually vibration_mm_s, sometimes with motor_current_a, and the cases describe it as a coupling or alignment-related vibration pattern. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#coupling][CASE-041][CASE-046] 
Soft foot or loose anchoring can point toward misalignment and vibration as well. [KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#baseplate]

faq.q: What is current imbalance in a motor?
faq.text: Current imbalance in a motor means the motor current is uneven across phases, often called phase-to-phase imbalance or current/load imbalance [KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#stator_windings][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#terminal_box][KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#motor]. It can point to issues such as stator winding insulation ageing, loose or corroded terminals, broken rotor bars, or load-related imbalance [KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#stator_windings][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#terminal_box][KB-XRAY-ELECTRIC_MOTOR#rotor][KB-XRAY-PROCESS_PUMP#motor]. The context includes synthetic asset examples where M-004 and M-005 are marked with current imbalance, but no live plant data or a specific selected asset is provided [ASSET-022][ASSET-023][DOC-APP-DATA].

faq.q: What causes a control valve position deviation?
faq.text:
Common causes in the context are friction or stiction, calibration drift, feedback linkage wear, air relay faults, loose mounting, actuator spring fatigue, abnormal load, supply pressure issues, and device alerts; these are investigation signals, not proof by themselves. [DOC-CONTROL_VALVE-CORE] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#spring] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#yoke] 
For control valves, the positioner, actuator spring, and yoke are named as likely contributors to position deviation. [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#spring] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#yoke] 
The fleet table also shows control valves with position deviation or calibration drift, including CV-003, CV-009, and CV-007. [ASSET-003] [ASSET-009] [ASSET-007]

faq.q: What is calibration drift?
faq.text:
Calibration drift means the asset’s measured position slowly stops matching the true or expected position over time, so the reading no longer lines up with the baseline or reference. [CASE-033] [KB-XRAY-CONTROL_VALVE#positioner] 
For CV-007, the evidence says “position calibration drift” with the next check to verify calibration, and its condition is watch with health 71. [DOC-ASSET-007] [ASSET-007] 
The context also says to review trend and events, compare to baseline, and follow approved safety and maintenance procedures. [CASE-033]

faq.q: What is a vibration sensor mounting issue?
faq.text: A vibration sensor mounting issue is a problem with how the sensor is attached to the machine, so the mounting is not giving a stable, rigid connection and the reading quality can drop [KB-XRAY-VIBRATION_SENSOR#mounting_stud, DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. Typical signs are loose mounting, wrong torque, signal drift, missing data, or poor signal quality, and it can reduce confidence in the vibration data [KB-XRAY-VIBRATION_SENSOR#mounting_stud, DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. The context also shows this as a mounting-quality signature with the next check being to inspect sensor mounting, while following approved safety and maintenance procedures [CASE-015]. For the fleet, VS-002 is listed with issue mounting issue and VS-003 is listed as normal [ASSET-029, ASSET-030].

faq.q: Why do data-quality issues lower confidence?
faq.text: Data-quality issues lower confidence because the confidence formula explicitly multiplies by one minus a data-quality penalty, so worse data reduces the final score [DOC-APP-DIAGNOSIS]. Poor signal quality, drift, missing data, or bad mounting also mean the sensor evidence is less reliable, so downstream confidence should drop [DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE]. The context also says stale or poor-quality data lowers confidence [DOC-APP-INTEGRATION].

faq.q: How was the 3D scan processed?
faq.text: The 3D scan was processed as a Gaussian-splat model of the equipment room, with the floor leveled by a RANSAC floor plane and the walls axis-aligned [DOC-APP-SCAN]. It is treated as approximately metric, but the scale was not surveyed [DOC-APP-SCAN]. The browser renders 1,669,970 splats with view-dependent colour as compressed chunks, while phones load the most important 730 thousand splats [DOC-APP-SCAN]. A 2D floor plan replaces the 3D view when WebGL 2 is missing, and an earlier corrupt file is not used [DOC-APP-SCAN].

faq.q: Does it work without a GPU or on a phone?
faq.text: Yes, it works without a GPU in the browser, because the 3D view falls back to a 2D floor plan when WebGL 2 is missing. On phones, it loads the most important 730 thousand splats, so it is supported there too [DOC-APP-SCAN]. The same planner runs in the browser as a JavaScript port, and the scan integrity notes say the environment is a Gaussian-splat scan with valid records [DOC-APP-NAV, DOC-APP-SCAN].
